intended_object: This is a proof device. It is the element x = ∑_{t∈T} t⁻¹·f(h_t) ∈ X, where h_t ∈ H is the factor with t = h_t·s_t relating the transversals T and S. It is used to show that the transfer (corestriction) of a crossed homomorphism does not depend on the choice of transversal, up to a principal crossed homomorphism. I inferred this from the docstring and from how the library uses it in `transferRaw_change` and `transferCrossed_change`.
explanation:
The definition is an intermediate quantity in the proof that corestriction on H¹ is well defined. Changing the transversal from T to S changes the transfer of f by the coboundary g ↦ x − g·x, with x = changeCoefficient (see `transferRaw_change`). This is then used to show that the cohomology class does not depend on the transversal. The expression has no standalone meaning in the literature. It is the usual bookkeeping term in the textbook proof that the transfer does not depend on the transversal.

The body matches its role: it sums t⁻¹·f(changeFactor T S t) over the finite transversal T. The sum is finite because H has finite index. Since this is an auxiliary construction rather than a mathematical object, it is not judged as faithful or too narrow.
